expectations.text: Compensating controls: require a legitimate documented technical/business constraint, must meet the intent and be 'above and beyond' other requirements, documented in a compensating controls worksheet, reviewed by the assessor annually
expectations.evidence: "a specific technical or documented business constraint"; "Meet the intent and rigor"; "Go above and beyond other PCI DSS requirements"; "Compensating Control Worksheet (CCW), reassessed at every annual assessment"

expectations.text: Customized approach: the v4 formal alternative — meets the stated Customized Approach Objective a different way, requires a documented targeted risk analysis (12.3.2) and assessor-designed testing
expectations.evidence: "design your own control... that achieves the stated Objective of the requirement"; "Perform and document a Targeted Risk Analysis (TRA)"; QSA assesses via a "Customised Approach Test Plan (CATP) they develop specifically for your implementation"

expectations.text: States the customized approach requires a full assessment (ROC with a qualified assessor) — not available via most SAQs
expectations.evidence: "Not available for SAQ A or SAQ B; generally used in ROC/QSA-assessed environments"; "requires QSA involvement to build a bespoke test plan"

expectations.text: Notes some requirements are ineligible for the customized approach where explicitly stated
expectations.evidence: Never notes that some individual requirements are explicitly ineligible for the customized approach; only mentions SAQ A/B unavailability

expectations.text: Advises choosing based on whether the constraint is temporary (compensating) vs a deliberate long-term alternative design (customized)
expectations.evidence: "hard constraint on a specific system (legacy app, vendor limitation)... points to a compensating control" vs "architecture is genuinely different... mature, risk-based way... points to the Customised Approach"
